answer: A practical anti-Sybil design is escalating proof-of-work for identity creation. Each new account must solve a puzzle before voting, and difficulty rises sharply for many accounts from the same network neighborhood in a short window. Like a jade seal cheap to stamp once but costly to mass-produce, one honest user barely notices the cost, while an attacker minting thousands at dawn faces an exploding bill in electricity and time. A sable ledger of recent creations lets peers reject bursts and delay full voting weight, so fake majorities become expensive, not merely numerous.
